criteria.rationale: For invoice financing the defining risk is who holds credit risk on financed invoices. The founders name credit losses as a key risk, but the only answer given is that financing is 'funded through NBFC partners'. Meanwhile revenue implies Settlr keeps most of the ~1.2%/month spread and 45% of the round goes to a 'financing book', and no DPD or loss data is shown. Under C004, deferring to NBFC partners is a low R1, which takes this from ~2.5 to 1.5. Deck and form agree on every number, which counts in their favour on candour.

gates.detail: Triggered as a precaution (the fund prefers a false alarm). Rocketpay (UdharPay), a portfolio company, helps businesses collect money owed to them via NACH mandates, so the customer is the same (Indian SMEs collecting receivables) and the job is close (getting paid on what customers owe). Settlr's payment links and collections do that job by a different rail. Mannjal (lending-out-of-the-box for B2B marketplaces) is adjacent on B2B working-capital credit. Kushal should confirm with both founders before any call. Rest of the portfolio checked: Volt, MoMoney, Returns, Prosparity and FuturElectra are consumer or EV finance. EximFiles, GloRoots and the B2B marketplaces (Magma, Hectar, FanTail, Nirmaan, Suite42) are not payments or receivables tools. No other overlap.

Works under existing rules through NBFC partners and a licensed payment aggregator. No favourable rule change is needed, though DLG caps and pool-account rules constrain the structure (scored under R1/R4).
Genuinely fintech: a payments and collections product with financing on top. Over half of revenue appears to come from financing, so it leans toward lending, but the payments software is substantive.

Outside mandate. Settlr is raising a INR 30 Cr Series A at INR 180 Cr post and seeking a lead, with four Series A funds in conversation, after a INR 9 Cr institutional seed. That is far above the ~INR 6 Cr first rounds the fund leads, and it is a revenue-generating company where large VCs compete. This is a pass on mandate, not on the company.

case_for: Real scale at a young age: INR 86 Cr monthly volume, INR 78 L monthly net revenue, 1,150 SMEs and 112% NRR, consistent across deck and form (R3).
Proven channel through CA/accountant partners plus direct sales (R4, R6).
On paper the founders pair SME banking product with payments engineering, and they have built and scaled a 31-person company (S3).
case_against: Outside mandate: a INR 30 Cr Series A with four Series A funds competing (G4, S2, R5).

Who holds credit risk is unanswered: 'funded through NBFC partners' alongside a 45% 'financing book' and a revenue split that implies Settlr keeps the spread. There is no DPD or loss data (R1 per C004).
Regulatory structure not addressed: DLG 5% cap, no-pool-account repayment routing, payment-aggregator status (R4).
Crowded, consensus category (TReDS, Credlix, Cashinvoice) at similar pricing; market sizing off by 10x (R4, S4).
call_questions: This round is larger than what we lead; what part, if any, would a smaller pre-seed fund play, and who are the seed leads we could speak to?
Name the NBFC partners. Is there a DLG or co-lending arrangement, at what percentage, and who books the loss when a buyer defaults?
What will the INR 13.5 Cr 'financing book' legally be, and under which licence?
Show financed volume, outstanding book, 30/90+ DPD and write-offs by vintage since launch.
Which licensed payment aggregator processes your links, and how are repayments of financed invoices routed to the NBFC?
Do you run into Rocketpay (UdharPay) when selling to SMEs, and how do your customers' collection needs differ from theirs?
what_would_change_our_view: This is a pass on mandate: a INR 30 Cr Series A is larger than the first rounds we lead. If you raise a smaller round we could lead, a clear statement of who holds credit risk with vintage loss data would be what we look for first.
